puppeteer_navigate.rationale: The tool can contact an arbitrary agent-supplied URL: `Navigate to a URL` and the `url` is a `URL to navigate to`, so it is a SINK because a request to an agent-chosen attacker host can carry agent-supplied data. The arbitrary URL also includes public attacker-controlled web pages, so output/browser state from the navigation can be UNTRUSTED; under the least-restrictive reading it can also include `file://`, `localhost`, or intranet URLs and therefore SECRET. The `launchOptions` are advertised as `PuppeteerJS LaunchOptions` and `If changed and not null, browser restarts`; because the schema leaves this object unrestricted and Puppeteer launch options may determine what executable/arguments are launched, the least-restrictive reading is HOSTEXEC. `allowDangerous` says dangerous options are rejected only when false for examples such as `--no-sandbox`, but the advertised text does not settle all LaunchOptions restrictions, so this is undetermined.

puppeteer_screenshot.rationale: The tool returns a screenshot: `Take a screenshot of the current page or a specific element`. Because the current page may be an attacker-controlled public web page, the screenshot content is UNTRUSTED. Because the current page may also be a non-public reachable page such as `file://`, `localhost`, or intranet content loaded by the browser, the screenshot can return SECRET data. The `encoded` option confirms the screenshot may be returned as text: `capture the screenshot as a base64-encoded data URI (as text)`.

puppeteer_click.rationale: The tool sends an agent-selected browser interaction to the current page: `Click an element on the page`, with `selector` as the `CSS selector for element to click`. Since the current page can be an attacker-controlled page reached by navigation, the page can observe the click or cause it to trigger network/state changes, making it a SINK for agent-supplied interaction. The advertised text does not say the tool returns page content, so SECRET/UNTRUSTED are not applied.

puppeteer_fill.rationale: The tool writes agent-supplied text into the current page: `Fill out an input field`; `selector` is the `CSS selector for input field` and `value` is the `Value to fill`. If the current page is attacker-controlled, page script or form submission can read that value, so this is a SINK. The advertised text does not say the tool returns page content, so SECRET/UNTRUSTED are not applied.

puppeteer_select.rationale: The tool writes an agent-supplied selection into the current page: `Select an element on the page with Select tag`; `selector` is the `CSS selector for element to select` and `value` is the `Value to select`. If the current page is attacker-controlled, it can observe the selected value, so this is a SINK. The advertised text does not say the tool returns page content, so SECRET/UNTRUSTED are not applied.

puppeteer_hover.rationale: The tool sends an agent-selected browser interaction to the current page: `Hover an element on the page`, with `selector` as the `CSS selector for element to hover`. Since the current page can be attacker-controlled, the page can observe the hover or trigger network/state changes from it, so it is a SINK for agent-supplied interaction. The advertised text does not say the tool returns page content, so SECRET/UNTRUSTED are not applied.

puppeteer_evaluate.rationale: The tool runs arbitrary browser-page JavaScript: `Execute JavaScript in the browser console`; `script` is `JavaScript code to execute`. It can return data from the current page, so if the page is attacker-authored public web content the returned result is UNTRUSTED, and if the page is a reachable non-public `file://`, `localhost`, intranet, or credentialed page, it can return SECRET data. The script can also send data to attacker-readable web destinations, so it is a SINK. This is not HOSTEXEC because the advertised execution is in the `browser console`, i.e. browser/page JavaScript rather than arbitrary host code.

value_conditions.effect: For puppeteer_navigate, dangerous LaunchOptions that reduce security are rejected for at least dangerous args such as --no-sandbox; default is false. The advertised text does not say this removes all launchOptions-related SECRET, SINK, UNTRUSTED, or HOSTEXEC concerns.
For puppeteer_navigate, dangerous LaunchOptions that reduce security are allowed.

notes: All judgments are based only on the advertised tool names, descriptions, schemas, and annotations. No source code or output schemas were provided.
The browser's current page is shared state across these tools; therefore interaction and screenshot/evaluate effects depend on pages previously reached by navigation.
